predecessors.name: Kingdom of Kashmir
predecessors.text: the Kashmir Valley and its hill dependencies, which Shah Mir took in the 1338-1339 war (Cliopatria's 1344 outline without Xinjiang, Xizang, Ladakh and Baltistan)

successors.name: Mughal Empire
successors.text: the Kashmir Valley: the Mughal page's infobox result is 'Annexation of Kashmir Valley'

ledger.x: 1339: Shah Mir takes the throne at Srinagar.

Pakhli and Swat taken in Shihabu'd-Din's reign (19 April 1354 - 6 June 1373): the page names them among his conquests; no year is given, the only date is his return to Srinagar 'around 1370', so the year is a bracket.
ledger.cp: page silent: the chiefs of Pakhli and Swat

ledger.x: Gilgit and the northern hill states defeated in Shihabu'd-Din's reign; the page gives no year (bracket 1354-1373, back at Srinagar 'around 1370').
ledger.cp: page silent: Gilgit and the northern hill states

ledger.x: Baltistan annexed in Shihabu'd-Din's reign: the page has the Maqpons of Baltistan as a tributary of Moghulistan and, after the victory over the Kashgaris, Baltistan and Ladakh 'annexed' into Kashmiri rule, with no year.
ledger.cp: page silent: the Maqpon rulers of Baltistan, a tributary of Moghulistan

ledger.x: Ladakh annexed in Shihabu'd-Din's reign: the Maryuls of Ladakh were a tributary of Tibet, then 'annexed' into Kashmiri rule after the Kashgar victory; no year given.
ledger.cp: page silent: the Maryul rulers of Ladakh, a tributary of Tibet

ledger.x: 1531: Kamran Mirza's Mughal army takes Srinagar.
1531: the Mughals are routed by Kaji Chak; the page gives no other year for the end.
December 1540: Haidar Dughlat, serving Humayun, attacks in November 1540 and Kashmir 'was formally annexed in December 1540'; infobox 'Mughal Interregnum: December 1540 - October 1551'.
1561: the Chaks replace the Shah Miris within the same sultanate.
Baltistan stands with the Mughals: the infobox lists 'Mughal Empire (supported by Maqpon Kingdom)'.
ledger.cp: page silent: the Maqpon Kingdom, which supported the Mughals

ledger.x: October 1586: the Mughals win the Battle of Hastivanj on 10 October 1586 and take Srinagar on 14 October 1586.
8 August 1589: the occupation ends in the annexation of the Valley.
The rest of the realm after the surrender: Gilgit, Pakhli, Swat, Ladakh and the hill states.
ledger.cp: page silent: no page assigns the lands outside the Valley after 1589

ledger.x: 8 August 1589: the dynasty ends and the Valley passes to the Mughals.

wars.name: Shah Mir-Lohara War
wars.outcome: Shah Mir took the throne and the Lohara line ended; the sultanate dates from 1339.

wars.name: Shihabu'd-Din's conquests and the Sutlej standoff with Firuz Shah
wars.outcome: Pakhli, Swat, Gilgit, Baltistan and Ladakh taken; a confrontation with Firuz Shah on the Sutlej ended in a peace under which, in the Shihabu'd-Din page, territories 'from Sirhind to Kashmir now belonged to the Kashmiri Empire' (the Kashmir Sultanate page…

wars.name: Kamran Mirza's invasion of Kashmir
wars.outcome: The Mughal army sacked Srinagar and was routed by Kaji Chak.

wars.name: Mughal Interregnum in Kashmir
wars.outcome: Haidar Dughlat, for Humayun, annexed Kashmir in December 1540 and beat Kaji Chak at Vahator on 13 August 1541; the interregnum ran to October 1551.

wars.name: Mughal conquest of Kashmir
wars.outcome: Mughal victory: the Battle of Hastivanj (10 October 1586) and the fall of Srinagar (14 October 1586); the Kashmir Valley annexed.
